newsitem.title: USA: SEC appoints David Nelson as Miami assistant chief.
newsitem.headline: SEC appoints David Nelson as Miami assistant chief.

text.p: David Nelson was appointed associate regional director in Miami for the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, SEC regional Director Charles Senatore said Wednesday.
Nelson will report directly to Senatore and supervise the SEC Southeast Regional Office's enforcement and regulatory programs.
He joined the agency as a staff attorney in Washington, D.C., in 1984 and later served as a special assistant federal prosecutor in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., and in New York City.
While in New York, he was one of five government lawyers who handled the criminal prosecution of Drexel Burnham Lambert, Michael Milken and Ivan Boesky.

Nelson has been with the SEC in Miami almost five years. Since 1995, he has served as co-head of its regional enforcment program and has pursued enforcement action involving violations of the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's rules on political contributions by municipal securities participants.

"He has had a distinguished career with the commission, tremendous experience in complex investigations and during his nearly five years in Miami has earned the respect of his colleagues," Senatore said.
